newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks mixed to firmer in light volumes.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks mixed to firmer in light volumes.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares traded mixed to firmer in light volumes on Tuesday with brokers saying they were beginning to see some foreign investors returning to the market.

"A lot of the industrial index's previous drive above the 8,000-mark was due to local institutional investors getting their positions right but external investors are now beginning to come back as the rains continue to fall," one broker said.

Some investors had taken to the sidelines ahead of the rains which started towards the end of November. Weather experts are predicting the rainy season to be near normal in the agriculture-led country.

On the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange on Tuesday, the key 57-share industrial index ended the day 13.13 points up at 8,029.53, pushed higher mainly by horticultural group Ariston's 50-cent rise to 1,700 as well as Alloys and furniture and clothing retailer Tedco's 25-cent gains each to 775 and 725 respectively.

Glass firm PG climbed 20 cents to 500, transport group Clan edged up 15 cents to 340 while 10-cent additions were recorded in rubber products manufacturer Acacia to 290 and seed manufacturer and distributor SeedCo to 220.

Among the losers, winery Afdis dropped 25 cents to 375 while battery manufacturer Chloride at 100, engineering firm Gullivers at 240, cement producer Porthold at 1,450 and sugar refinery ZSR at 1,380 all shed 10 cents.

Minings continued lacklustre but one broker said he expected gold prices to pick up on physical demand of the yellow metal over Christmas but said base metal prices were likely to remain in the doldrums into the New Year.
"There's no real reason for base metal prices to push up in the near future. They should continue bouncing around in the doldrums," he said.
On the local bourse's mining board on Tuesday, Wankie Colliery shed 10 cents to 430 while gold producer Ashanti, nickel miner Bindura and copper firm Mhangura traded at previous levels.
The seven-counter mining index lost 4.39 points to 1,110.74.
